N s/^[ \t]*}/ \ \ - name: content-volume \ \ mountPath: /usr/share/nginx/html \n}/g b :next_line }' app_pod.yaml # A safer approach for step 2 is to find the end of the first container's definition and append the mount. sed -i '/containers:/ { # This attempts to find the end of the first container block and append the mount. :append_mount N /^\s*}/ { # Check if we are in the first container block (assuming 2 spaces indentation) /^\s* - name: web-server/ { s/^[ \t]*}/ \ \ volumeMounts: \ \ - name: content-volume \ \ mountPath: /usr/share/nginx/html \n}/g } b :append_mount } }' app_pod.yaml # Step 3: Append the new file-writer container definition after the last container block. cat >> app_pod.yaml <Hello World' > /data/index.html"] volumeMounts: - name: content-volume mountPath: /data EOF # Re-saving the file after modifications (The above commands modify in place, but a final verification/write step is good practice if the shell supported it cleanly) # Step 4: Apply the modified configuration kubectl apply -f app_pod.yaml"}
